question:
A concave spherical mirror forms a **real** image of a point object on a movable screen placed on the principal axis (object and screen are on the same side of the mirror). Initially, the object is at the centre of curvature and the image is sharply formed on the screen at the same location.

The object is then moved $4\,\text{cm}$ towards the mirror and the screen is adjusted to obtain a sharp image again (screen position $S_1$).

Keeping the screen at $S_1$, the object is moved a further $6\,\text{cm}$ towards the mirror. To obtain a sharp image again, the screen must now be moved $15\,\text{cm}$ farther away from the mirror (still on the object side).

Using Cartesian sign convention, the focal length of the mirror is:
